cards.headline: Church, Neighbors Rally Around Family After Port St. Lucie House Fire
cards.teaser: A fire that tore through the garage of a Carmelite Street home injured a renter and displaced his family, but members of a Fort Pierce church showed up to help them salvage belongings and begin cleanup.
cards.body:
A fire that spread through the garage of a Port St. Lucie home Friday afternoon injured a father and displaced his family, while neighbors and church members rallied to help with the cleanup. The fire broke out on Carmelite Street in the Northport Village neighborhood. St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded around 1:30 p.m. and arrived to find heavy fire coming from the garage.

According to the family, the fire started in the kitchen before spreading through the garage. They say a propane tank later exploded, causing additional damage and impacting a neighbor's garage doors across the street. When firefighters extinguished the flames, they left behind significant damage, including a charred garage door, blackened walls and belongings covered in soot.

Renter Nigel Laidlow was inside the home when the fire broke out and suffered burns to his legs. He was transported for medical treatment. "I don't even know how to describe it. It was really surreal," Laidlow said. "I would've never thought a little fire would turn into this."

By Saturday, family photos, furniture and other belongings were spread across the front yard as loved ones worked to salvage what they could. Members of the Fort Pierce Seventh-day Adventist Church spent the day helping move and sort through the damaged items. "We have a really strong support system, especially from my church," Laidlow said. Despite the loss, he said he is grateful his family survived. "This right here is something not anybody would like to deal with. Not in a lifetime," he said. The family is now focused on recovering and determining its next steps, and the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Flooding at Port St. Lucie's California and Savona Boulevards Costs Pizza Shop Thousands
cards.teaser: Repeated flooding at the California and Savona boulevards intersection forced Estella Pizzaria to close early and halt deliveries this week. The city says a sensor pilot program is starting now, but a larger drainage fix for the Oak Hammock neighborhood is still years off.
cards.body:
Flooding at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie has cost Estella Pizzaria thousands of dollars in lost revenue, according to an employee at the shop. The restaurant sits in a shopping plaza near the intersection, which turned into standing water earlier this week before receding.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria, said the flooding was severe enough that neighbors joked about calling it the California River. "It becomes like an island around here," Dascoli said. The shop had to close early on Thursday because of the water. "It's an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved," he said.

Dascoli said customers could not reach the shop and orders could not go out during the flooding. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

The city of Port St. Lucie is starting a pilot program that will place water level sensors at flood-prone locations, according to Scott Samples with the city. Samples said the sensors will send alerts to Public Works and police when an area sees rapid flooding, allowing crews to respond faster. He said a longer-term fix is planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, where a large-scale drainage project would add two new retention ponds and baffle boxes to collect runoff, along with raising sections of the roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Samples said the project is currently in the data collection phase before design work begins. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said.

cards.headline: Red Cross Aids Port St. Lucie Family After Northwest Carmelite Street Fire
cards.teaser: Four people, including two children, received emergency assistance after a house fire on Northwest Carmelite Street in Port St. Lucie. Red Cross volunteers also helped a Riviera Beach fire victim the same day.
cards.body:
The American Red Cross assisted four people, including two adults and two children, after a house fire at a home on Northwest Carmelite Street in Port St. Lucie. The organization's Disaster Action Team volunteers responded to the fire as part of a news release issued Friday, Oct. 9, which detailed assistance provided to a total of five people displaced by two separate house fires within a 12-hour period.

The second fire struck a home on West 28th Street in Riviera Beach, where one adult received help from Red Cross volunteers. The Red Cross did not release information about what caused either fire or the extent of the damage at either location.

Red Cross Disaster Action Team volunteers are specially trained to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For the family displaced from the Northwest Carmelite Street home, volunteers provided emergency financial assistance, health and mental health services, and recovery support. All Red Cross disaster assistance is provided free of charge and funded through donations.

Residents who want to support disaster relief efforts for families like the one displaced in Port St. Lucie can donate at redcross.org/donate. The Red Cross also offers information about home fire safety and preparedness at redcross.org/homefires, resources aimed at helping Treasure Coast residents reduce their risk of displacement from future house fires.

hero.headline: MARTY Bus Service Halted Without Warning Across Martin County
hero.body:
MARTY public transit service in Martin County came to an abrupt halt Thursday, leaving riders who depend on the system without their regular transportation while county officials scramble for a fix. Martin County officials said they received no advance warning that service would stop that day.

According to the county, MARTY's operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had requested a significant increase in its contract. The company says rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs have caused significant financial losses since it began running the service in July 2025. Negotiations between the county and the operator failed to produce an agreement. County officials said the company gave 180 days' notice to terminate its contract about two weeks ago, but then notified the county Thursday morning that it was immediately discontinuing service.

George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said officials are exploring both short-term and long-term solutions to restore service. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." County officials said they are working with community partners, including United Way, to help residents affected by the shutdown. No timeline has been set for when MARTY operations will resume, and officials said they will post updates on social media and notify residents once a solution is reached.

The sudden suspension left riders stranded across Martin County. Leticia Chaclan waited for a bus in Stuart on Thursday that never came, and said she was unaware the service had been suspended until a reporter told her. Chaclan said she has ridden the bus for years and called it essential for many in the community. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don't have a driver's license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It's very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don't drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don't drive, and we go everywhere to shop." Steven Godell, another rider affected by the shutdown, said he was on his bicycle Thursday after the MARTY bus did not show up that morning. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested on Murder Charge in August Shooting Death of Ex-Girlfriend
hero.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man is being held without bond after his Oct. 5 arrest on a first-degree murder warrant in the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on the warrant, which accuses him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic. A judge had signed the warrant in August.

Deputies were called to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead. Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend.

According to the arrest affidavit, a coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death. The coworker also said Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Surveillance footage reviewed by detectives showed a person they identified as Waggle in the area around the time of the shooting, as well as walking through the area before and after it. That footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which investigators later recovered.

Investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch near the crime scene. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. Waggle remains held without bond at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on the first-degree murder charge.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Rolls Out Flood Sensors After California Boulevard Flooding Hurts Business
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is launching a pilot program to install water level sensors at flood-prone intersections after recent flooding at California and Savona boulevards cost a nearby pizza shop thousands of dollars in lost business. The intersection flooded badly earlier this week, with standing water covering the roadway like a lake before receding.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said the flooding turns the surrounding shopping plaza into an island. "We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." The shop had to close early on Thursday because of the flooding, and Dascoli said customers could not get in and orders could not go out. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City officials say they are responding with both immediate and long-term measures. Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the new pilot program will place water level sensors in flood-prone areas to alert Public Works and police when rapid flooding begins. "There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker," Samples said.

For a longer-term fix, Samples pointed to a large-scale drainage project planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project calls for two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and raised sections of roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Samples said the project is currently in the data collection phase and has not yet moved into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said. Dascoli said the flooding is "an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved."

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Teen Dies After Being Struck Walking to School on PSL Boulevard
hero.body:
A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student has died after being struck by a vehicle while walking to school in Port St. Lucie. The Port St. Lucie Police Department said the crash happened near the intersection of SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Squirrel Avenue on the morning of Oct. 8.

A preliminary investigation found the teen was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near the edge of the roadway when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. Detectives are continuing to examine the circumstances surrounding the crash, and the investigation remains active.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department extended its condolences to the student's family, friends and classmates, saying in a statement that its thoughts are with them during this difficult time.

cards.headline: Grease Fire Sparks Propane Explosion at Port St. Lucie Home
cards.teaser: A grease fire in a garage touched off a propane tank explosion that hurled debris across a Port St. Lucie street Friday afternoon, destroying most of a family's belongings and briefly sending the father to the hospital.
cards.body:
A grease fire inside the garage of a Port St. Lucie home ignited a propane tank explosion Friday afternoon that destroyed nearly everything a family of four owned. St. Lucie County Fire District received the initial call at 1:24 p.m. for a fire at a home in the 100 block of Carmelite Street after neighbors spotted smoke and called 911.

Neighbors said the man who lives at the home told them he had been cooking when a grease fire broke out in the garage, where a propane tank was stored. The blast launched the tank out of the garage, across the street, and into a neighbor's garage. Marina Cheong, who lives a few doors down, said she was in her backyard when she saw heavy smoke and ran toward the home to help, only to be stopped by the explosion. "And then there was explosion, very loud, loud explosion, and debris started flying everywhere," she said.

Neighbor Rob Roadman said he heard the blast before he saw what caused it. "I heard a huge explosion. At first, I thought maybe it's a transformer or something, but it was much, much, much louder than that," he said. "I thought it was an air raid. It was not a casual thing. My house shook," he added. Cheong described a similar reaction, saying, "I thought that the whole house had exploded. It was very loud." Roadman said he checked on the father shortly afterward. "I asked the dad if he was OK, and he goes, 'Yeah.' But you could tell he wasn't. Who wouldn't be?" Roadman said.

The father was briefly hospitalized but returned to the home a few hours later to join family and friends sifting through the wreckage. They found little worth saving. A family member said they consider themselves lucky that no one was seriously injured and credited a strong community and church for helping them through the aftermath.

cards.headline: Church Members Help Port St. Lucie Family After Carmelite Street House Fire
cards.teaser: A renter suffered leg burns escaping a fire that tore through his Port St. Lucie home, and members of a Fort Pierce church are now helping the displaced family clean up.
cards.body:
A fire tore through the garage of a home on Carmelite Street in Port St. Lucie's Northport Village neighborhood Friday afternoon, injuring a man and displacing his family. St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded around 1:30 p.m. and arrived to find heavy fire coming from the garage. According to the family, the fire started in the kitchen before spreading through the garage, and a propane tank later exploded, causing additional damage and impacting a neighbor's garage doors across the street.

Renter Nigel Laidlow was inside the home when the fire broke out and suffered burns to his legs. He was transported for medical treatment. "I don't even know how to describe it. It was really surreal," Laidlow said. "I would've never thought a little fire would turn into this."

Firefighters extinguished the flames, but significant damage was left behind, including a charred garage door, blackened walls and belongings covered in soot. By Saturday, family photos, furniture and other belongings were spread across the front yard as loved ones worked to salvage what they could. Members of the Fort Pierce Seventh-day Adventist Church spent the day helping move and sort through the damaged items. "We have a really strong support system, especially from my church," Laidlow said.

Despite the loss, Laidlow said he is grateful his family survived. "This right here is something not anybody would like to deal with. Not in a lifetime," he said. The family is now focused on recovering and determining its next steps, and the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

hero.headline: Martin County Employee Rescues Three Girls From Rip Current at Bob Graham Beach
hero.teaser: A county worker with lifeguard training pulled three girls from a rip current at the unguarded Jensen Beach access point, then drove one girl showing signs of distress to a nearby lifeguard station for help.
hero.body:
A Martin County employee helped rescue three girls caught in a rip current Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach in Jensen Beach, an unguarded stretch of shoreline. Amy Offenbach, who works in Martin County's Growth and Development Department and is an avid surfer, said she arrived at the beach around 2 p.m. to surf when she noticed three girls about 25 yards offshore holding onto the same surfboard.

Offenbach said something about the scene caught her attention right away. "The ocean could be very gentle and calm, but it can also be very heavy and crash very hard," she said. She grew concerned when one of the girls appeared distressed. "That kind of struck me as strange," Offenbach said. "The other one seemed a little agitated." Moments later, a girl on the beach told Offenbach she believed her friends needed help. "By that time the girls were waving in the water like they needed help, so immediately I just went into rescue mode," Offenbach said.

Offenbach and a friend paddled out to the girls. When she reached the group, she said one girl appeared to be in serious distress. "I looked at her, and she seemed kind of dazed and confused," Offenbach said. "I said, 'Get up on the board.'" Offenbach gave her surfboard to two of the girls and told them to hold on and kick toward shore, then placed the third girl on her soft-top board and paddled her back to the beach. Offenbach, who has some lifeguard training, quickly recognized the girl needed medical attention. "The girl that I rescued said that she blacked out under the water," Offenbach said. "She inhaled water, and she had a severe headache." Because Bob Graham Beach has no lifeguard on duty, Offenbach drove the girl to a nearby lifeguard station, where an ambulance was called.

Offenbach said she hopes the rescue reminds beachgoers to understand ocean conditions before entering the water. She encourages people to swim at guarded beaches when possible, check rip current forecasts, and use flotation devices or boards when appropriate. "I'm just really happy that I was in the right place at the right time," she said. Offenbach said she has not been able to reconnect with the girl she rescued or learn more about her condition. "It can be very treacherous," Offenbach said of the ocean. "Treacherous."

cards.headline: Martin County Scrambles to Restore MARTY Bus Service After Sudden Shutdown
cards.body:
Martin County's public transit system, MARTY, abruptly stopped running Thursday, leaving riders who depend on it for medical appointments, work and shopping trips without transportation. County officials said they received no advance warning before the service halted.

MARTY's operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had asked the county for a significant increase in its contract, citing rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs that the company says have caused significant financial losses since it took over the service in July 2025. Negotiations between the county and the company failed to produce an agreement. County officials said the company gave formal notice about two weeks ago that it would terminate its contract in 180 days, but then notified the county Thursday morning that it was ending service immediately.

George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said the county is pursuing both short-term and long-term fixes to get buses running again. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." The county has not given a timeline for when service will resume and says it will post updates on social media as a solution develops. Officials said they are also working with community partners, including United Way, to help residents affected by the shutdown.

The sudden halt caught riders off guard. Leticia Chaclan of Martin County waited for a bus in Stuart on Thursday that never arrived, and said she had been unaware the service was suspended until a reporter told her. Chaclan said she has ridden MARTY for years and called it essential for many in the community, especially those without a driver's license. "We really need the bus," she said. cards.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested on Murder Charge in Girlfriend's Shooting Death
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man is being held without bond on a first-degree murder charge in connection with the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant accusing him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic. He was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies were called to the 500 block of 1st Street in August after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about him before her death and said Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the scene around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area both before and after the shooting. That footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which investigators later recovered.

Near the crime scene, investigators found a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch. A Ruger pistol was recovered on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the arrest affidavit. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle in August, and he remains held without bond following his October arrest.

cards.headline: Martin County Employee Rescues 3 Girls From Rip Current at Bob Graham Beach
cards.teaser: A Martin County Growth and Development Department employee pulled three girls from a rip current at the unguarded Bob Graham Beach in Jensen Beach, then drove one of them to a lifeguard station for medical help.
cards.body:
A Martin County employee helped rescue three girls caught in a rip current Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach in Jensen Beach. Amy Offenbach, who works in Martin County's Growth and Development Department, said she arrived at the beach around 2 p.m. to surf when she noticed three girls about 25 yards offshore holding onto the same surfboard.

Offenbach, an avid surfer, said something about the scene immediately caught her attention. "The ocean could be very gentle and calm, but it can also be very heavy and crash very hard," she said. She grew concerned when one of the girls appeared distressed. "That kind of struck me as strange," Offenbach said. "The other one seemed a little agitated." Moments later, a girl on the beach told Offenbach she believed her friends needed help. "By that time the girls were waving in the water like they needed help, so immediately I just went into rescue mode," Offenbach said.

Offenbach and a friend paddled out to the group. When she reached the girls, Offenbach said one of them appeared to be in serious distress. "I looked at her, and she seemed kind of dazed and confused," Offenbach said. "I said, 'Get up on the board.'" She gave her surfboard to two of the girls and told them to hold on and kick toward shore, then placed the third girl on her soft-top surfboard and paddled her back to the beach. Offenbach, who has some lifeguard training, quickly recognized the girl needed medical attention once they reached land. "The girl that I rescued said that she blacked out under the water," Offenbach said. "She inhaled water, and she had a severe headache." Because Bob Graham Beach is unguarded, Offenbach drove the girl to a nearby lifeguard station, where an ambulance was called.

Offenbach said she hopes the rescue reminds beachgoers to understand ocean conditions before entering the water. She encouraged people to swim at guarded beaches when possible, check rip current forecasts, and use flotation devices or boards when appropriate. "I'm just really happy that I was in the right place at the right time," she said. Offenbach said she has not been able to reconnect with the girl she rescued or learn more about her condition. She said the ocean demands respect despite the enjoyment it brings her. "It can be very treacherous. Treacherous," Offenbach said.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Search for Driver in Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Man, 63
hero.teaser: A 63-year-old Port St. Lucie man remains in critical condition with severe head trauma after a hit-and-run crash near NW University and NW California boulevards. Police are reviewing surveillance footage and asking the public for tips.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police are searching for the driver who struck a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie resident in a hit-and-run crash early Friday morning near the intersection of NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. The man was found unconscious in the roadway at about 12:56 a.m. with severe head injuries and significant bleeding.

He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment and remains in critical condition, police said.

Detectives have obtained surveillance video from a nearby business that captured the incident and are continuing to collect and evaluate additional footage as they work to identify the vehicle and driver involved. Investigators are still working to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the crash.

Police are asking anyone who was driving in the area around the time of the crash, witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or other video footage to come forward. Authorities said even information that seems insignificant could help identify the driver and move the investigation toward a resolution. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Flooding at California, Savona Boulevards Costs Pizza Shop Thousands
cards.teaser: Chronic flooding at the Port St. Lucie intersection of California and Savona boulevards forced Estella Pizzaria to close early this week, and city officials say a lasting fix is still years away.
cards.body:
Flooding at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie has cost a nearby pizza shop thousands of dollars in lost revenue, and city officials say a permanent solution is still in the early planning stages. Floodwaters receded this week after turning the intersection into what looked like a lake earlier in the week.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said the shopping plaza where the restaurant sits becomes isolated during heavy flooding. "We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." The flooding forced the shop to close early on Thursday, cutting off customers and delivery drivers alike. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City officials said they are rolling out a pilot program to install water level sensors at flood-prone locations around Port St. Lucie. Scott Samples, speaking for the city, said the sensors would send alerts to Public Works and police when an area starts flooding rapidly, allowing crews to respond faster. The sensor program is aimed at addressing immediate response times rather than the underlying drainage problem.

A longer-term fix is planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, where the city intends to build two new retention ponds and install baffle boxes to capture runoff. The project also calls for raising sections of the roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Samples said the project is currently in the data collection phase and has not yet moved into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Targets California-Savona Flooding With Drainage Project, Sensor Alerts
hero.body:
Repeated flooding at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie has forced a nearby pizza shop to close early and lose thousands of dollars in revenue, and city officials say a long-term fix is coming but will take time. The city is also starting a pilot program using water level sensors at flood-prone areas to speed up emergency response.

The intersection flooded badly again this week, turning the roadway into what neighbors called a lake. Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said employees joked about calling it the "California River" because the shopping plaza where the restaurant sits becomes an island during heavy flooding. Dascoli said the shop had to close early on Thursday because customers could not get in and delivery drivers could not get out safely.

"We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City representative Scott Samples said Port St. Lucie is rolling out a pilot program that places water level sensors in flood-prone areas around the city. The sensors will send alerts to Public Works and police when an area is seeing rapid flooding, allowing crews to respond faster. Samples said the city's long-term solution is a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood that includes two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and raised sections of roadway at California and Savona boulevards. The project is currently in the data collection phase before moving into design. Samples called it one of the city's highest capital investment priorities but said it will take time to complete. Dascoli said the flooding problem is ongoing and needs to be resolved.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Teen Hit Walking to School Remains Critical, No Charges Yet
cards.teaser: A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student remains in critical condition after being struck from behind near a construction zone on Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard. The driver, a 72-year-old man, stopped and returned to the scene after realizing he had hit a person rather than a construction barrel.
cards.body:
A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student remains in critical condition after being struck by a vehicle while walking to school Wednesday morning, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. No charges have been filed as the investigation continues.

Police said the crash happened around 6 a.m. near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue. The student was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard, near the edge of the roadway in an area marked by construction barrels, when he was struck from behind.

Investigators said the vehicle involved was a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. Police said the driver initially believed he had struck a construction barrel and did not realize he had hit a person. He later made a U-turn at the next safe location, returned to the scene, activated his hazard lights and found the teenager unconscious on the side of the roadway.

The driver has remained cooperative with investigators, and police said they have not observed any apparent signs of impairment, though officials noted that assessment is preliminary and could change as the investigation continues. The student, identified only as a freshman at Treasure Coast High School, suffered life-threatening injuries. Anyone who witnessed the crash or has dash-camera, surveillance or other video footage from the area around the time of the incident is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

cards.teaser: A 63-year-old Port St. Lucie man remains in critical condition after being hit by a driver who fled the scene near NW University Boulevard. Police are reviewing surveillance footage and asking witnesses to come forward.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police are searching for a driver who struck a 63-year-old pedestrian and fled the scene early Friday morning, leaving the man in critical condition. The victim, a Port St. Lucie resident, was found unconscious in the roadway near the intersection of NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard at about 12:56 a.m.

Police said the man was suffering from severe head trauma and significant bleeding when he was found. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment and remains in critical condition.

Detectives have obtained surveillance video from a nearby business that captured the incident and are continuing to collect and evaluate additional footage as they work to identify the vehicle and driver involved. Investigators are still working to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the crash.

Port St. Lucie police are asking anyone who was driving in the area at the time of the crash, witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or other video footage to come forward. Officials said even seemingly minor details could help investigators identify the driver and resolve the case. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Rolls Out Flood Sensors as California-Savona Drainage Fix Awaits
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is launching a pilot program using water level sensors at flood-prone spots around the city after repeated flooding at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards cost a nearby pizza shop thousands of dollars in lost business. The flooding turned the intersection into what looked like a lake earlier this week, with the water receding only in recent days.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said the shopping plaza where the restaurant sits becomes isolated during heavy rain. "We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." The shop had to close early on Thursday because of the flooding, and Dascoli said customers could not get in and delivery orders could not get out. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," he said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City representative Scott Samples said Port St. Lucie is starting the sensor pilot program to monitor flood-prone areas in real time. "There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker," Samples said. The sensors would give city crews earlier warning so they can respond to flash flooding before it worsens.

Samples said the long-term solution for the California and Savona corridor is a large-scale drainage project planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project calls for two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect stormwater runoff, and raised sections of roadway at the California and Savona intersection. The project is currently in its data collection phase and has not yet moved into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said. Until the Oak Hammock project advances, businesses like Estella Pizzaria remain vulnerable to the kind of flash flooding that shut them down this week.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Man Charged With Murder in August Shooting Death of Ex-Girlfriend
cards.teaser: Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested on a first-degree murder warrant in the shooting death of Dawn Marie Kriskewic, who was found in the roadway on 1st Street in Vero Beach. Surveillance footage and items recovered near the scene led investigators to the charge.
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in the August shooting death of Dawn Marie Kriskewic, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond.

Deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death and said Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area both before and after the shooting. Investigators said the footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which they later recovered.

Near the crime scene, investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest bearing a "security" patch. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle on Aug. He was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Tests Water Sensors as California, Savona Flooding Drains Business
hero.body:
Flooding at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie has receded after turning the roadway into what neighbors jokingly called the "California River" earlier this week. Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria in the shopping plaza next to the intersection, said the flooding forced the business to close early on Thursday and has cost it thousands of dollars in lost revenue.

"We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." He said customers could not reach the shop and orders could not go out while the water was high. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City representative Scott Samples said Port St. Lucie is starting a pilot program that will install water level sensors at flood-prone areas around the city. The sensors would send alerts to Public Works and police when an area is seeing rapid flooding, allowing crews to respond faster. "There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker," Samples said.

Samples said the long-term fix for the area is a large-scale drainage project planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project calls for two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and raised sections of roadway at California and Savona boulevards. He said the project is still in the data collection phase before the city moves on to design work. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said. For Dascoli and his coworkers at Estella Pizzaria, the flooding remains a recurring problem that disrupts business every time the rain comes. "It's an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved," Dascoli said.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Hunt Driver Who Hit Man Near NW University, NW California Boulevards
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police are searching for the driver who struck a 63-year-old resident early Friday morning and left the scene, leaving the man in critical condition with severe head trauma. Officers found the victim unconscious in the roadway near the intersection of NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard at approximately 12:56 a.m. Police have since confirmed he was the victim of a hit-and-run crash.

The man was suffering from severe head trauma and significant bleeding when he was found. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment and remains in critical condition.

Detectives have obtained surveillance video from a nearby business that captured the incident and are continuing to collect and review additional footage as they work to identify the vehicle and driver involved. Investigators say they are still working to determine the circumstances surrounding the crash.

Police are asking anyone who was driving in the area around the time of the crash, anyone who may have witnessed the incident, or anyone with dashcam or other video footage to come forward. Authorities said even information that seems insignificant could help investigators identify the driver and resolve the case. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves assisted-living site plan despite contamination concerns
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the major site plan for a 150-unit assisted-living facility near a petroleum-contaminated property, even as residents cite an engineering letter showing cleanup plans had to be revised because of the project. The development still needs further agency review before construction can begin.
cards.body:
Sandpiper Bay residents who had asked Port St. Lucie and St. Lucie County fire officials to intervene in a proposed assisted-living development next to a known petroleum-contaminated property are now reacting to news that the city has approved the project's major site plan. The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the major site plan for the facility, known as PSL Westmoreland ALF, in September, despite ongoing objections from nearby residents about the environmental history of the neighboring contaminated property.

The proposed facility is a three-story, 150-unit assisted-living project with a memory care component, planned for 7.1 acres within the Rivella planned unit development along Southeast Morningside Boulevard near Southeast Westmoreland Boulevard. Construction has not begun. The developer must still submit construction plans for technical review, followed by additional agency reviews, including one from the South Florida Water Management District, before building can start.

Residents' concerns center on an engineering letter that provides new detail about the contamination issue. The letter, from BTEX Engineering, discussed a March 2026 meeting with environmental officials about the neighboring property and said the proposed remediation approach should be changed because of concerns about surrounding properties, including the planned assisted-living facility. The letter said vapors would need to be captured during the remediation process.

Resident David Lipps said the issue is not about what is being built on the site, arguing that nearby businesses and other facilities could also be affected by environmental concerns. Resident Charlie D'Agata said residents have raised objections at City Council meetings for about two years and questioned why a developer would be allowed to build near a property he described as contaminated. Residents say they have contacted the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Florida Department of Health in an effort to get answers about the site.

The environmental history of the neighboring property and the extent of any potential impact on surrounding land remain central questions for residents seeking more information. With the major site plan now approved, residents say they want clearer answers about the contamination and how any risks would be addressed as the project advances through the remaining review steps.

cards.headline: 2 Arrested After Woman Shot At While Fleeing Fort Pierce Attack
cards.teaser: A woman escaped an attack on South Sixth Street and was shot at as she drove away. Fort Pierce police have arrested 18-year-olds Keibin Lopez-Godoy and Kailee Yurubi in connection with the shooting.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police have arrested two 18-year-olds in connection with an attack and shooting that sent a woman fleeing for her life on South Sixth Street earlier this month. Keibin Lopez-Godoy faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide, and Kailee Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact.

The case began on Saturday, October 3, when Fort Pierce police officers responded to South Sixth Street at 7:12 a.m. after the victim called 911 to report that someone was shooting at her. Investigators said the woman had gone to the address to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship. When she arrived, several people ran out of the residence and began attacking her, according to police.

The victim managed to break free, get into her vehicle, and drive away from the scene, police said. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and opened fire on her vehicle, according to investigators.

Police said a second person was arrested for allegedly driving the shooter away from the scene after the attack. Lopez-Godoy and Yurubi were both identified as the suspects taken into custody in the case.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound Woman Charged After Deputies Say She Buried Live Kittens
cards.teaser: A 37-year-old Hobe Sound woman faces four felony animal cruelty charges after deputies say she buried kittens alive in her yard during what family members described as a mental health crisis.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound woman is facing four felony animal cruelty charges after Martin County deputies say she buried live kittens in her yard at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested 37-year-old Alba Luz Chavez on four counts of aggravated animal cruelty after investigators said they found two live kittens and two dead kittens buried on the property. Deputies were called to the home Thursday night for what family members described as a mental health crisis.

Family members told deputies Chavez believed the cats were demons and had killed several animals earlier in the week. According to the arrest affidavit, Chavez had allegedly told residents of the home she killed two kittens on Monday. Three juveniles living at the residence told deputies Chavez had appeared to be experiencing a mental health episode for most of the week. The juveniles said they locked three surviving kittens inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday evening, and when they returned around 6 p.m., they found Chavez had forced her way into the room and the kittens were gone.

Investigators said Chavez initially refused to tell family members where the animals were. While speaking with deputies, Chavez allegedly said, “If you want the cats, you will need gloves, a red bag and a shovel,” and directed them to an area on the property. Deputies dug and found two live kittens buried underground inside plastic Publix bags, according to the affidavit. They later uncovered two deceased kittens that appeared to be in the early stages of decomposition. Detectives searched for a third missing kitten but were unable to locate it.

During an interview, Chavez told investigators she had been cleaning her house and referred to the cats as “very ugly,” according to the affidavit. Investigators wrote that Chavez also made statements indicating she did not want black cats and suggested kittens of different colors “had different fates.” The affidavit states Chavez later began singing instead of answering additional questions. The two surviving kittens were taken to a pet emergency center for treatment. A veterinarian told investigators the kittens were about three weeks old and very weak, and said it was too early to determine whether a lack of oxygen while confined inside the plastic bags had caused brain damage or other medical complications. The two deceased kittens are expected to undergo necropsies to determine their exact causes of death. Chavez was booked into the Martin County Jail on the four felony counts and is being held without bond.

hero.headline: Sheriff: Deputies Heard Kittens Crying Underground in Hobe Sound Burial Case
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek on Friday gave new details on the arrest of a Hobe Sound woman accused of killing two kittens and burying two others alive, revealing that deputies heard the animals crying from beneath the ground during a backyard search. Alba Chavez, 36, faces four felony counts of animal torture after deputies said she buried kittens up to 3 feet underground at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park, with two kittens rescued alive and two found dead. A fifth kitten remains missing despite repeated searches of the property.

Deputies responded to the mobile home park Thursday night after several minors inside the home called 911 to report that Chavez had killed two kittens on Monday, placed them in the trash and later buried them in the backyard. The children, fearing for three remaining kittens, had locked them inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday night. When they returned, they found the bedroom door forced open and the kittens gone, prompting the call to law enforcement. Deputies found Chavez standing in the roadway, and she reportedly admitted to killing the two kittens, telling deputies she believed the animals had demons, calling them ugly and saying she did not want black or brown cats in the home.

Chavez then led deputies to the backyard where the kittens had been buried. "She took them to the backyard where our deputies started digging frantically trying to recover what they believed to be three live kittens and two dead kittens," Budensiek said. As deputies dug through the rain-soaked ground, they heard cries coming from underground. Two kittens were pulled out alive and rushed to an emergency veterinary facility, where they were being treated for dehydration. The sheriff said veterinarians were also concerned about possible injuries from lack of oxygen while the animals were buried, and he said the kittens could still die from their injuries despite being rescued. The two kittens killed Monday were found dead at the burial site.

Chavez was arrested and charged with four counts of animal torture involving pain, serious injury or death, corresponding to the two kittens found dead and the two found alive. She is being held without bond at the Martin County Jail and also has an immigration hold. Investigators have not determined how the first two kittens died or established a motive for Chavez's actions. Budensiek said Chavez initially cooperated with deputies and led them to the burial site but later stopped answering questions about how the animals were killed. The sheriff said deputies had previously responded to calls involving Chavez's mental health but had received no prior animal cruelty complaints at the residence. Additional charges could be filed if the missing fifth kitten is found dead. The Florida Department of Children and Families became involved following the incident, and the children were released to their father, who lives locally. Officials said resources were available to help the children cope with what happened.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested in August Shooting Death of Ex-Girlfriend
cards.teaser: Matthew Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on a first-degree murder warrant in the death of Dawn Marie Kriskewic, who was found shot in the roadway on 1st Street in Vero Beach in August.
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in connection with the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was taken into custody Oct. 5 on an active warrant accusing him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic. He is being held without bond at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, where he was booked.

Deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach in August after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death and said he had previously threatened consequences if she called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Surveillance footage reviewed by detectives showed a person they identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area both before and after it occurred. Investigators said the footage also captured him discarding a shirt, which they later recovered.

Near the crime scene, investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest bearing a "security" patch. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the arrest affidavit. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle in August, and he remained at large until his arrest in October.

hero.headline: Sheriff: Deputies Heard Kittens Crying Underground in Hobe Sound Burial Case
hero.teaser: Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek revealed new details about the arrest of a Hobe Sound woman accused of burying kittens alive, saying deputies heard cries coming from the ground as they dug to rescue two surviving animals.
hero.body:
Deputies digging through a rain-soaked backyard in Martin County heard kittens crying from as deep as 3 feet underground, leading to the rescue of two animals while two others were found dead, Sheriff John Budensiek revealed Friday. The discovery came during the investigation into 36-year-old Alba Chavez of Hobe Sound, who is accused of killing two kittens earlier in the week and burying two more alive in the backyard of a mobile home park. Budensiek held a news conference to lay out new details of the case, including the frantic digging that led deputies to the surviving animals.

According to the sheriff's office, deputies were called to the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park Thursday night after several minors inside the home dialed 911, reporting that Chavez had killed two kittens on Monday, thrown them in the trash and later buried them in the yard. Worried about three other kittens still in the home, the children locked them in a bedroom before leaving for dinner that evening. When they returned, Budensiek said, the bedroom door had been forced open and the kittens were gone, prompting the children to call authorities.

When deputies arrived, Chavez was standing in the roadway and admitted to killing the two kittens, the sheriff's office said. She told deputies she believed the kittens had demons, called them ugly and said she did not want black or brown cats in her home. She then led deputies to the backyard, where the animals had allegedly been buried. "She took them to the backyard where our deputies started digging frantically trying to recover what they believed to be three live kittens and two dead kittens," Budensiek said. As they dug, deputies heard crying coming from underground. Two kittens were pulled out alive, while the two Chavez allegedly killed Monday were found dead. A fifth kitten has not been located despite repeated searches of the property.

The surviving kittens were rushed to an emergency veterinary facility for treatment of dehydration, and veterinarians are also watching for possible injuries caused by oxygen deprivation while they were buried. Their survival is not guaranteed. Chavez was arrested and charged with four counts of animal torture involving pain, serious injury or death, covering the two kittens found dead and the two rescued alive. She is being held without bond at the Martin County Jail and also has an immigration hold. Investigators have not determined exactly how the first two kittens died or what motivated the killings, and Budensiek said Chavez stopped answering questions about the deaths after initially cooperating. The sheriff noted deputies had responded to past calls involving Chavez's mental health but had no previous animal cruelty complaints at the home. Additional charges are possible if the missing kitten is found dead. The Department of Children and Families got involved, and the children were released to their father.

cards.headline: Vero Beach man charged with murder in August shooting death of ex-girlfriend
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond on allegations he killed Dawn Marie Kriskewic.

Deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead. Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death and that Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings.

Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the scene around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area both before and after the shooting. Investigators said the footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which was later recovered. Near the crime scene, investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest bearing a "security" patch. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the arrest affidavit.

A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle in August. He was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on Oct. 5 and remains held without bond.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Seek Help Identifying Critically Injured Man Found on Roadway
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police are asking the public for help identifying a man found unconscious with severe head injuries on a city roadway early Friday morning. Passing drivers discovered him around 1 a.m. near Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where he remains in critical condition.

Police said the man suffered severe head trauma and significant bleeding and did not have identification with him. He is believed to be middle-aged or older and is known to walk in the area overnight.

Investigators described him as wearing a green, blue and white T-shirt, black shorts, multicolored Brooks athletic shoes, a gray Adidas baseball cap and Wiley X sunglasses. He was also carrying a pink umbrella with a black handle.

Police are asking anyone who recognizes the man to call 772-871-5000. Investigators also want to hear from witnesses and anyone with dashcam or security camera video from the area around the time he was found.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Police Arrest Two After Woman Attacked, Shot At on South Sixth Street
cards.teaser: A woman escaped an attack outside a Fort Pierce home and was shot at as she drove away. Police have arrested two 18-year-olds, one on an attempted first-degree homicide charge.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police have arrested two 18-year-olds after a woman was attacked at a South Sixth Street home and then shot at as she fled the scene in her car. Keibin Lopez-Godoy faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide, and Kailee Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact, both 18.

According to the Fort Pierce Police Department, officers responded to South Sixth Street at 7:12 a.m. on Saturday, October 3, after the victim called 911 to report that someone was shooting at her. Investigators determined the woman had gone to the address to talk with her boyfriend about their relationship. When she arrived, several people ran out of the residence and attacked her.

Police said the victim managed to break free, get into her vehicle and drive away. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and opened fire on her car, according to police. A second suspect is accused of driving the shooter away from the scene afterward.

Lopez-Godoy was arrested on the attempted first-degree homicide charge for allegedly firing the shots at the victim's vehicle. Yurubi was arrested on the accessory after the fact charge for allegedly helping the shooter leave the area following the attack. The Fort Pierce Police Department has not released additional details on the relationship between the suspects and the victim's boyfriend or on the status of any other people who may have been involved in the initial attack at the home.

cards.headline: MARTY Bus Service Suspended Across Martin County After Contract Dispute
cards.teaser: MARTY public transit stopped running Thursday after its operator abruptly ended service amid a contract dispute with Martin County. Riders without cars were left stranded as officials scramble for a fix.
cards.body:
MARTY public transit service across Martin County came to an abrupt halt Thursday, leaving riders who depend on the buses without their regular transportation. County officials said they received no advance warning that service would stop that day. MARTY's operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had requested a significant increase in its contract with the county, citing rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs that the company says have caused significant financial losses since it began running the service in July 2025.

Negotiations between the county and the company failed to produce an agreement. County officials said Martin County Transit LLC gave a 180-day notice to terminate its contract roughly two weeks ago, but then notified the county Thursday morning that it was discontinuing service immediately. The sudden shutdown left residents who rely on MARTY with no regular way to get around the county.

George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said the county is pursuing both short-term and long-term solutions to restore service. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." County officials said they are working with community partners, including United Way, to help residents affected by the suspension. No timeline has been given for when MARTY operations could resume, and officials said they will post updates on social media and notify residents once a solution is reached.

The impact was immediate for riders who count on the bus daily. Leticia Chaclan, of Martin County, waited for a bus in Stuart on Thursday that never came. She said she had not known MARTY was suspended until a reporter told her. Chaclan said she has ridden the bus for years and called it essential for many in the community. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don't have a driver's license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It's very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don't drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don't drive, and we go everywhere to shop." Steven Godell, another rider affected by the suspension, said he rode his bicycle Thursday after the MARTY bus did not arrive that morning. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said.

hero.headline: Sheriff: Deputies Heard Kittens Crying Underground in Hobe Sound Case
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said Friday that deputies digging through a rain-soaked backyard in Hobe Sound could hear kittens crying from as deep as three feet underground, a detail that emerged as he laid out new information about the arrest of 36-year-old Alba Chavez. Chavez faces four felony counts of animal torture involving pain, serious injury or death after deputies said she killed two kittens earlier in the week and later buried two more alive in the yard of her home at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. Two kittens were pulled from the ground alive, while the two Chavez allegedly killed days earlier were recovered dead.

According to the sheriff's office, deputies were called to the mobile home park Thursday night after several minors living in the home dialed 911 to report that Chavez had killed two kittens on Monday, thrown them away and then buried them in the backyard. Worried about three kittens still alive, the children locked them in a bedroom before leaving the house for dinner that evening. When they got back, Budensiek said, they found the bedroom door had been forced open and the kittens were gone, which prompted them to contact law enforcement.

Deputies found Chavez standing in the roadway when they arrived, and she admitted to killing the two kittens, according to the sheriff's office. She told deputies she thought the kittens were possessed by demons, called them ugly, and said she did not want black or brown cats in her home. She then walked deputies to the backyard, where they began searching for three kittens believed to still be alive along with the two that had already died. "She took them to the backyard where our deputies started digging frantically trying to recover what they believed to be three live kittens and two dead kittens," Budensiek said. As they dug, deputies heard crying coming from beneath the ground and ultimately rescued two kittens, while the two killed earlier in the week were found dead. A fifth kitten has not been located despite multiple searches of the property.

The two kittens pulled from the ground were rushed to an emergency veterinary clinic, where they were treated for dehydration, and Budensiek said doctors are also watching for complications from lack of oxygen while buried underground. Investigators have not determined how the first two kittens died or established a motive for the killings, and Chavez stopped answering questions about the deaths after initially cooperating. The sheriff noted deputies had responded to past calls involving Chavez's mental health but had no previous animal cruelty complaints tied to the address. Chavez is being held without bond at the Martin County Jail and has an immigration hold, and additional charges are possible if the missing kitten is found dead. The children involved were placed with their father following contact from child welfare officials.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested on Murder Charge in Dawn Kriskewic Shooting Death
cards.teaser: Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested on a first-degree murder charge in the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, Dawn Marie Kriskewic, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said.
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in connection with the August shooting death of a woman, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. The warrant accuses him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic, whom investigators identified as his former girlfriend.

Deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR. She was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

According to the sheriff's office, a coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death. The coworker also told investigators that Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area before and after the shooting. Investigators said the footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which they later recovered.

Investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch near the crime scene. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle in August.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Approves Assisted-Living Project Amid Contamination Concerns
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council has approved the major site plan for a 150-unit assisted-living facility planned next to a property with a history of petroleum contamination, despite objections from nearby residents who say they still lack answers about potential risks. The project, known as PSL Westmoreland ALF, is planned for 7.1 acres within the Rivella planned unit development along Southeast Morningside Boulevard near Southeast Westmoreland Boulevard. The three-story facility would include assisted-living units and a memory care component.

Construction has not begun. The developer must still submit construction plans for technical review, followed by additional reviews involving the South Florida Water Management District and other agencies.

A group of residents has opposed the project, pointing to the environmental history of the neighboring contaminated property and what it could mean for future residents of the facility. Resident David Lipps said the issue is not about what is being built on the site, arguing that nearby businesses and other facilities could also be affected by environmental concerns. Resident Charlie D'Agata said residents have raised objections at City Council meetings for about two years and questioned why a developer would be allowed to build near a property he described as contaminated. Residents say they have contacted the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Florida Department of Health seeking more information about the site.

An engineering letter adds new weight to those concerns. The letter, from BTEX Engineering, discusses a March 2026 meeting with environmental officials about the neighboring property and states that the proposed remediation approach should be changed because of concerns about surrounding properties, including the planned assisted-living facility. The letter said vapors would need to be captured during remediation. The full environmental history of the neighboring property and the extent of any potential impact on surrounding land remain central questions for residents as the project moves toward construction review.

hero.headline: MARTY Bus Service Halted Countywide After Martin County Contract Dispute
hero.body:
MARTY public transit service across Martin County stopped abruptly Thursday after its operator, Martin County Transit LLC, notified the county it was immediately discontinuing service, leaving residents without their regular transportation. County officials said they received no advance warning that service would stop that day.

According to the county, Martin County Transit LLC had requested a significant increase in its contract, citing rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs that the company says have caused significant financial losses since it began operating MARTY in July 2025. Negotiations between the county and the company failed to produce an agreement. County officials said the company gave formal notice about two weeks ago that it would terminate its contract in 180 days, but then told the county Thursday morning that it was ending service immediately.

George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said the county is now working on both short-term and long-term solutions to restore service, though he did not offer a timeline. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." County officials said they are working with community partners, including United Way, to assist residents affected by the shutdown, and they plan to post updates on social media as a solution develops.

The suspension has already disrupted daily routines for riders who depend on MARTY. Leticia Chaclan, a Martin County resident who has ridden the bus for years, waited in Stuart on Thursday for a bus that never came and said she had not known service had been suspended. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don't have a driver's license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It's very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don't drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don't drive, and we go everywhere to shop." Another rider, Steven Godell, said he resorted to riding his bicycle Thursday after the bus failed to show up that morning. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound Woman Charged, Held Without Bond in Cat Burial Case
cards.teaser: Alba Luz Chavez faces four felony counts of aggravated animal cruelty after deputies said she buried kittens alive during a mental health crisis. A third kitten remains missing.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound woman has been arrested and charged with four felony counts of aggravated animal cruelty after deputies said she buried kittens alive in her yard, believing they were demons. The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested 37-year-old Alba Luz Chavez this week after investigators said they dug up two live kittens and two dead kittens buried on a property at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. Chavez is being held without bond at the Martin County Jail. Deputies had previously confirmed finding the four animals during a search that recovered two survivors alive and two dead.

Deputies were called to the home Thursday night for what family members described as a mental health crisis. Relatives told deputies Chavez believed the cats were demons and had killed several animals earlier in the week. According to the arrest affidavit, Chavez had told residents of the home she killed two kittens on Monday. Three juveniles living at the residence told deputies Chavez had appeared to be experiencing a mental health episode for most of the week. The juveniles said they locked three surviving kittens inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday evening, but when they returned around 6 p.m., they found Chavez had forced her way into the room and the kittens were gone.

Investigators said Chavez initially refused to tell family members where the animals were. While speaking with deputies, Chavez allegedly said, "If you want the cats, you will need gloves, a red bag and a shovel," and directed them to an area on the property. Deputies dug there and found two live kittens buried underground inside plastic Publix bags, according to the affidavit. They later uncovered two deceased kittens that appeared to be in the early stages of decomposition. Detectives searched for a third missing kitten but were unable to locate it.

During an interview, Chavez told investigators she had been cleaning her house and referred to the cats as "very ugly," according to the affidavit. Investigators wrote that Chavez also made statements indicating she did not want black cats and suggested kittens of different colors "had different fates." The affidavit states Chavez later began singing instead of answering additional questions. The two surviving kittens were taken to a pet emergency center for treatment. A veterinarian told investigators the kittens were about three weeks old and very weak, and said it was too early to determine whether a lack of oxygen while confined inside the plastic bags had caused brain damage or other medical complications.
